dedupe_keys.name: ankara forecasting ambulance demand and planning station capacity for prehospital emergency medical services

description: This case study forecasts demand for ambulances in Ankara, the capital of Türkiye, and works out how many ambulances each station needs to meet response time targets. The authors published it as an open-access journal article using records of 943,412 cases handled by 139 ambulance stations. Demand was forecast at district level, focusing on seven districts, with Holt-Winters, ARIMA, multilayer perceptron, neural network autoregression and LSTM methods, and Monte Carlo simulation then accounted for uncertainty in call volumes and response times to find the number of ambulances required at each station. Coverage is the city and province of Ankara. The article is free under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial licence, but the incident data are not published. Caveats: results apply to the study period and districts analysed, and the station capacities are model recommendations, not implemented changes. The study found that combining forecasting with simulation identified the optimal ambulance numbers per station to meet response time targets and argued that accurate forecasting is essential for timely prehospital care. Simulation uses: a worked example of demand forecasting and Monte Carlo capacity planning for emergency response services. Related records: the Region Zealand dispatch trends study (case_study-region-zealand-ambulance-dispatch-response-time-trends) documents rising demand elsewhere.
